stem: Leela presses the tip of a metal nail into soft clay. Kabir presses the flat face of a wooden block into the same clay with the same downward force.

parts.text: Which claim about pressure on the clay is correct?

options.text: The nail tip produces greater pressure because the same force acts on a smaller area.
The wooden block produces greater pressure because it covers more clay.
At the same force, doubling the contact area doubles the pressure.
Both produce the same pressure because the downward force is the same.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Pressure is force per unit area; for the same force, a smaller contact area gives higher pressure.

teacher.key_rationale: Pressure is force per unit area. The nail tip has a smaller area than the block face, so the same force gives greater pressure at the tip. Larger area lowers pressure; doubling area does not double pressure.
